summary:
Fire Atlas is a tool to harmonise and display data collected by MODIS and VIIRS sensors. It is designed to be as fast and efficient even on the lowest end software

It harmonises the data from 4 sensors and provides a visualisation. It also provides historical medians and anomalies. It also can show distribution of fire power over months
details:
Data:

Data is downloaded from NASA FIRMS and converted into a custom binary format to reduce reading times and compressed with xz to reduce bandwidth usage

All data is uploaded to google drive and is accessed from there

Website Server:

The website server is hosted on AWS LightSail and runs Debian, it runs a rust based server using Axum and Tokio, HTTPS is provided by Let's Encrypt

Website Backend:

All processing happens locally on the client device.

The engine is written in Swift and compiled to WASM to improve performance in loop heavy tasks. GPU acceleration uses WebGPU and since WASM doesn't have a WebGPU API, it uses JS. Data is not copied between the two, data is directly written into the memory address. The entire software is heavily optimised. When the first prototype was made, it benchmarked at around 33 secs excluding download, today it sits at 5 secs including download on a MacBook Pro M4 Max

MCP Server:

The Debian system has a specific user called fire-reader, the client connects to it with a python script that can by downloaded by curl -fL -o fire-atlas-mcp-source.tar.gz https://54.66.142.30/mcp/source and then unzip it. The client needs SSH installed on it to connect as the connection uses SSH. This is mainly for simplicity and hardening is provided by locking down that user's capabilities to only read what needs to be read and blocking the execution of any files. This is written in a mix of swift and rust.
